comparator.sourceNotes: The current TU/e programme and degree-structure pages establish the 180-EC bachelor, its behavioural-science and behavioural-research core, three technical specialisations, challenge-based work, elective space and Bachelor Final Project. The September 2025 NVAO accreditation report reproduces the current curriculum table introduced for starters from 2023-2024 and phased through the third year in 2025-2026. That table accounts for 180 EC as 36 five-credit quarter slots, with the Bachelor Final Project occupying two slots. It identifies the named Psychology & Technology, research-methods, data, ITEC and challenge courses, six technical-specialisation slots (30 EC), 45 EC of electives and a 10-EC final project. Robotics is instantiated by the neutral official-order rule; the route component is preserved as one 30-EC restricted specialisation block because the public curriculum table labels its six positions as Technical Course rather than supplying a current route-specific list.

Each route has thirteen courses not present in the other.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest programme is a defensible psychology-and-human-technology response with behavioural methods, data, AI and robotics. A second coherent curriculum follows the explicit responsible-design, technology-adoption and social-consequences cluster and passes all qualitative and pairwise distinctness rules. The remaining Living and built-environment direction was tested but UCR lacks the environmental-psychology and built-environment sequence needed to sustain it as a third 24-course programme.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Introduction to Brain & Behavior supplies broad psychological and neuroscientific foundations, but not the target course's dedicated technology framing.
Social Psychology directly addresses social influence and behaviour; TU/e also gives environmental psychology dedicated coverage.
Neurobiology provides a biological account of brain and behaviour.
Higher Order Functions studies attention, memory, executive functions and decision processes.
Perception & Action closely addresses perception, action and sensorimotor interaction.
Medical & Health Psychology addresses behaviour and wellbeing, but not the full digital-tools component.
Introduction to Programming provides the computational foundation used in behavioural technology work.
Introduction to Data Science develops applied data preparation and visualisation.
Research Methods & Statistics covers research design, experiments, surveys and inference.
Statistics & Experimental Methods provides psychology-specific experimental and multivariate methods.
Market Research includes applied user research, but is not an equivalent qualitative psychology project.
Advanced Research Seminar develops evidence synthesis and independent research design.
Probability & Statistics supports quantitative behavioural analysis but is not a dedicated research project.
Mathematical Methods covers calculus and quantitative modelling.
Robotics addresses sensing, movement and autonomous systems, but one UCR course cannot reproduce the 30-EC TU/e robotics specialisation.
Decision-making in AI examines intelligent-agent behaviour; TU/e adds explicit human-centred design and evaluation.
AI Ethics directly addresses responsible design, fairness, privacy and accountability.
Consumer Product Design provides one team-based design and prototyping experience, but not TU/e's multidisciplinary engineering challenge.
Introduction to Sociology addresses institutions and social relations; TU/e adds dedicated social-network analysis.
UCR distributes societal and ethical analysis across several courses; no single scheduled course reproduces this ITEC component.
TU/e preserves 45 EC of genuine elective space; the displayed UCR pathways are complete fixed examples.
TU/e requires a 10-EC Bachelor Final Project. UCR optional independent research is shown separately.

notes.text: TU/e integrates behavioural science and research with a 30-EC technical specialisation, named research projects, multidisciplinary challenge-based engineering, Impact of Technology courses, 45 EC of genuine electives and a required Bachelor Final Project. UCR offers strong psychology, cognitive science, research methods, data, AI, computer vision, robotics, design, communication and social analysis, but neither route reproduces TU/e's six-course engineering specialisation, sensors-and-control formation, repeated challenge projects, dedicated environmental-psychology and built-environment sequence or compulsory final project.
